mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% per month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 97 for three consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and lowers profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and accelerating inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12mo MA and CPIAUCSL > 12mo MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based demand collapse, which reduces economic activity and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both fall > 1% MoM in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for four consecutive months signals deep labor market distress, which suppresses consumer demand and corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.8%) in at least 50% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) below -1% combined with a concurrent decline in housing starts (HOUST) below -5% signals a coordinated collapse in residential demand, which disproportionately affects construction and materials sectors and drags equity indices lower over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -1% AND HOUST MoM < -5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 25% of triggered months.
